text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.71% today to $427.34, continuing a rough two-week slide of over 10%. The immediate trigger was the company's quarterly earnings announcement and a leadership change on November 3rd, along with release of its quarterly financial report. While the stock had climbed sharply on October 30th, today's decline suggests the earnings results and forward guidance disappointed investors or raised concerns about the company's direction under new leadership.

The broader backdrop weighs on refining stocks right now. U.S. oil is trading at $103 per barrel while refineries are running at 92.8% capacity, and storage levels for gasoline and diesel remain healthy — conditions that normally support refiner margins. However, a CNBC report from late October cautioned that Big Oil earnings guidance matters more than current results, and a Democratic Congress could shift energy policy away from traditional oil refining toward renewables, adding political uncertainty to the sector's outlook.
